method: Authenticated loopback /chatbot/chat; synthetic level-6 test identities; self-verification by Codex

live_answers.question: What is gold's historical seasonal tendency in the 15 trading days leading up to a December FOMC meeting?
live_answers.reply:
TradeWave cannot calculate this exact event-relative study because it lacks historical December FOMC dates and trading-session calendars. Its ordinary windows use calendar days, so using 15 calendar days would not answer the question.

A fixed-date gold study can be run instead, clearly labeled as a calendar-date approximation.

live_answers.question: Filter out any seasonal setups that have an upcoming earnings release during the next month.
live_answers.reply: I can't apply an earnings-exclusion filter with Tara's current tools. I can help inspect supplied earnings dates for named candidates, but an estimated or missing date does not establish that a setup is earnings-free.

live_answers.question: Scan my Growth watchlist and tell me which tickers are entering a seasonal buy zone next week.
live_answers.reply: I can’t retrieve a personal “Growth” watchlist through Tara, so I can’t scan its members directly. Send the ticker symbols and I’ll identify which have historical seasonal entry windows next week; dates are research evidence, not guaranteed buy signals.

live_answers.question: Show me the detrended year-by-year seasonal chart for SPX over the last 20 years.
live_answers.reply: I can't create a detrended year-by-year chart with Tara's current tools. I can show the supported Trend Chart or yearly return bars instead, but those are not a detrended chart.

live_answers.question: Add the top AAPL seasonal setup for next week to my calendar with entry and exit reminders.
live_answers.reply: I can't create calendar events or entry/exit reminders directly. For a saved pattern, use Portfolio Manager's notification icon to open Google Calendar setup and complete the prompts there; I can help research the setup and verify its dates first.

limitations: All 20 prompts tested for knowledge retrieval; five capability-boundary answers tested live. Not an exhaustive end-to-end financial-answer evaluation; no new underlying tools; no browser changes.
